exercises.instruction: Window or forecast? Pick what the sentence means

options: Even if there’s traffic, I’ll come.
Because of the traffic, I didn’t come.
items.explanation: Trafiğe rağmen — the traffic was already there, you can see it out the window. It’s a fact, so “despite.”

options: Even if it snows, I’ll come.
If it snows, I won’t come.
items.explanation: yağsa bile — there’s no snow yet, it’s a forecast. So “even if.”

items.prompt: How do you say “despite the cold”?
items.explanation: Before rağmen there’s always the dative -(y)A. soğuk → soğuğa: k between vowels becomes ğ.

items.prompt: How do you say “Even though it snowed, I came”?
items.explanation: “Even though” is a fact: the snow really fell. A fact needs rağmen: kar yağmasına rağmen. -sA bile is only “even if.”

items.translation: Today, despite the snow, Kızılay is packed.
items.explanation: rağmen wants the dative case: kar + a = kara.

items.translation: Yesterday, despite the cold, I didn’t put on a jacket.
items.explanation: soğuk + a: the voiceless k between vowels softens into ğ. You get soğuğa.

items.translation: Even if the bus doesn’t come, I’ll walk.
items.explanation: gelmese is a forecast, the conditional form. After it comes bile, not rağmen.

items.translation: Even if it’s expensive, I’ll buy it.
items.explanation: The last vowel in olsa is a. So da, not de.

items.text: Çok ___ bile bu işi bir günde bitiremezsin.
items.translation: Even if you work a lot, you won’t finish this in a day.
items.explanation: bile needs the conditional form before it: çalış + sa + n = çalışsan.
her şey + e = her şeye. Then rağmen, then the main part: mutluyuz.

items.translation: Even if I’m late, wait for me.
items.explanation: Nobody’s late yet, it’s a forecast: geç kalsam bile.

items.translation: Despite the traffic, I came on time.
items.explanation: The traffic happened — that’s a fact. trafik + e = trafiğe, then rağmen.

exercises.instruction: Find the bad take and reshoot it

items.explanation: Without the dative, rağmen doesn’t work: kar + a = kara.
yorgunluk + a: k → ğ, ending -a. You get yorgunluğa.

items.prompt: Even though it was cold, we went out.
items.explanation: “Even” is not always bile. It really was cold, so it’s a fact: soğuğa rağmen.
Before rağmen a whole action becomes a noun: yağ + ma + sı + na. Like “despite it raining,” not “despite it rained.”

exercises.instruction: A week on the calendar: fill each day with the right form
exercises.description: A calendar of a week in Ankara. Each card is a fact (window) or a forecast. The learner picks the missing piece of the sentence.

items.explanation: The traffic happened — a fact. trafik + e = trafiğe, then rağmen.
No snow yet — a forecast. bile needs the conditional: yağsa.
There was a line, the ticket got bought. After the dative kuyruğa comes rağmen.
Nobody’s late yet. After geç kalsam comes bile.
olsam: the last vowel is a, so da. Written separately.
bu gets an n before the ending: buna rağmen — despite this.

items.statement: “Even though it was noisy, I fell asleep” = “Gürültü olsa bile uyudum.”
items.explanation: “Even though” is a fact, and -sA bile is only “even if.” The right way: Gürültüye rağmen uyudum.

items.prompt: How do you say “even if the bus doesn’t come”?
items.explanation: Negation in a forecast goes through -mA-: gelmese bile. gelse bile means “even if it comes.”

items.prompt: Sen gitmesen ___ ben giderim. What goes in the gap?
items.explanation: The last vowel in gitmesen is e. So de.

items.statement: “Her şeye karşın” means almost the same as “Her şeye rağmen.”
items.explanation: karşın is the same realist, just more formal. Also the dative, also a fact.

items.prompt: Despite the bad weather, we went for a walk.
items.explanation: The weather happened — that’s a fact. hava + y + a = havaya, then rağmen.
